akhfash:3-3.t: He said: ﴿يَسْتَحِبُّونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: He joined the verb with "على", as they said "ضَرَبُوهُ في السيف" (they struck him in the sword), meaning "بالسيف" (with the sword). That is because all these particles are used for joining [verbs], and they are also omitted, as in the Arabs' saying "نَزَلْتُ زيداً", meaning "نَزَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ" (I stayed with him as a guest).

akhfash:16-16.t: He said: ﴿مِّن وَرَآئِهِ﴾, i.e. "in front of him". He said ﴿وراء﴾ only meaning that it is beyond what he is in, as you say to a man "هذا مِن ورائِكَ", i.e. "it will come upon you", and "هُوَ مِنْ وَراءِ ما أَنْتَ فيه" (it is beyond what you are in), because what you are in has been like that, so it is behind it. And He said ﴿وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌ﴾ in this sense, i.e. it was beyond what they were in.

akhfash:18-18.t: He said: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾. It is as though He said "and among what We relate to you is the likeness of those who disbelieved", then proceeded to explain, as He said ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾; and this is frequent.

akhfash:22-22.t:
He said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَنْ دَعَوْتُكُمْ﴾. This is a disjoined exception, as you say "ما ضَرَبْتُهُ إلّا أَنَّهُ أَحْمَقُ" (I did not strike him; it is only that he is a fool), and it is the one in the sense of "لكنّ" (but).
And He said ﴿وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُصْرِخِيَّ﴾: the yāʾ of the first-person possessive took fatḥa because before it is the quiescent yāʾ of the plural that was in "مُصْرِخِيَّ", so it had to be vowelled, since kasra is [too close] to yāʾ. We have heard that al-Aʿmash read (بِمُصْرِخيِّ) with kasra; this is a solecism (laḥn) which we have not heard from any of the Arabs or the grammarians.

akhfash:24-24.t: He said: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً﴾: accusative by (ضَرَبَ), as though He said "and Allah struck a good word as a likeness".

akhfash:25-25.t: He said: ﴿تُؤْتِيۤ أُكُلَهَا﴾, and like that is ﴿أُكُلُهَا دَآئِمٌ﴾. "الأُكُلُ" is food, and "الأَكْلُ" is the action (eating).

akhfash:31-31.t:
He said: ﴿لاَّ بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلاَ خِلاَلٌ﴾, and in another place (ولا خَلَّةٌ). "الخِلالُ" is the plural of "الخُلَّةِ" (friendship), as you say "جُلّة" and "جِلال" (date-baskets), "قُلَّة" and "قِلال" (jars). The poet said [in the mutaqārib metre, and it is the twenty-fifth poetic witness]:
وكيفَ تُواصِلُ مَنْ أَصْبَحَتْ * خَلاَلَتُهُ كَأَبي مَرْحَبِ
(How can you keep company with one whose friendship has become like Abū Marḥab [i.e. the shadow, fickle]?)
If you wish, you may make "الخِلال" a maṣdar, because it is from "خَاللْتُ" (I befriended), like "قَاتَلْتُ"; and the maṣdar of this is only "الفِعال" or "المُفاعَلَة".

akhfash:34-34.t:
He said: ﴿وَآتَاكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ﴾, i.e. "He gave you of everything you asked Him something", and He left "something" implied, just as He said ﴿وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, i.e. "she was given of everything in her time something". Some said: "This is only by way of multiplication (hyperbole)", like your saying "هُوَ يَعْلَمُ كُلَّ شيء" (he knows everything) and "أتاه كلُّ الناسِ" (all the people came to him), when he means some of them; and likewise ﴿فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾. Others said: "There is nothing that some people have not asked Him for, so He said ﴿وَآتَاكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ﴾, i.e. of everything you asked Him, He has given some of you something of it and given another something of what he asked".
Some read ﴿مِّن كُلٍّ﴾ with tanwīn; he says ﴿مِّن كُلٍّ﴾ and then says "[what] you did not ask Him for", as you say "قَدْ سَأَلْتُك مِنْ كُلٍّ" (I have asked you for some of everything) and "قَدْ جَاءَنِي مِنْ كُلٍّ" (there came to me some of everything), because "كُلّ" may stand alone.

akhfash:37-37.t:
Likewise He said: ﴿إِنَّيۤ أَسْكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ﴾; he says: "I have settled some people of my offspring". The bāʾ entered on "وادٍ" (valley) as you say "هو بِالبَصّرَةِ" and "هو في البصرة" (he is in Basra).
And He said ﴿تَهْوِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾: they claimed that in exegesis it means "تَهْواهُم" (it longs for them).

akhfash:43-43.t: He put ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise ﴿مُقْنِعِي﴾, as though He said: "their eyes stare, hastening". He made "الطَرْفَ" (the gaze) apply to the group, as He said ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾.

akhfash:47-47.t: He said: ﴿مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ﴾: He annexed it to the first and put the second in the accusative by the verbal force. It is not good to annex it to the second, because that would separate the muḍāf from the muḍāf ilayhi, and that is not good. It must be annexed because the alif [of tanwīn] has been dropped; had it been "مخلفا", He would have put both in the accusative, and that is permissible in speech. Like it is "هذا مُعْطي زَيْدٍ دِرْهَما" and "مُعْطٍ زيداً دِرْهَما" (this one is giving Zayd a dirham).
